To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
disseminated neoplastic and haemocytic lesions were detected in cockles Ceratostoderma edule that had suffered from high mortality in the northern rías of Galicia (Spain).
disseminated neoplastic lesions and large foci of haemocytosis are common in cockles Ceratoderma edule affected by high mortality in Galician rias and could have contributed to mortality.
2 pathological conditions, disseminated neopla sia and foci of heavy hemocytic infiltration, were found in the cockle in areas affected by mass mortality in the Galician rias.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the first description of disseminated neoplastic lesions in cockles and with the occurrence of large foci of haemocyte infiltration, which is a pathological condition not previously reported in cockles.
the first report of the occurrence of disseminated neoplastic lesions in C. edule.
the description and prevalence of 2 severe pathological lesions in cockles from northern Galician rias and with the possible relationship between these lesions and high mortality.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cause of high cockle mortality in Galician rias remains unknown.

the observed high mortality in C. edule was caused by 2 pathological conditions, disseminated neopla sia and haemocytic infiltration, that could be considered as a new disease syndrome in this species.
both conditions were associated with mortality in cockles from Galicia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the observed pathological conditions could be related to the high cockle mortality.
the observed mortality was not caused by a single factor but rather by a combination of several stress factors that could be associated with the environmental conditions of the area.
the cockles in northern rias are affected by a high prevalence of severe and potentially lethal conditions that could be the cause of their high mortality.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the occurrence of disseminated neoplastic lesions in the cockle C. edule is a new record in Europe, although the condition has been previously reported for other bivalves, including the Pacific oyster, Crassostrea gigas, in Japan, and the Manila clam, Ruditapes philippinarum, in Korea.

the high mortality in cockle beds in Galicia is associated with the presence of disseminated neoplastic cells and foci of heavy infiltration with haemocytes, which are probably the consequence of the same underlying cause.
, although the cause of the high mortality in the northern rias remains unknown, the high mortality could be the result of the combined action of several stressors.
